title: Favoritpudding (Favorite Pudding)
description: A pudding made with yeast, wheat flour, and lemon.

ingredients.name: For glaze: 2 parts white wine, 1/2 kg sifted powdered sugar

steps: Warm the milk and dissolve the yeast in a little of it.
Make a dough of flour, milk and yeast, work it well and set it to rise.

When the dough has risen well, work it again; add the whisked eggs, sugar, grated lemon peel, (blanched and grated almonds), salt and the rest of the flour, and lastly knead in the washed and wrung butter.
Work the dough for at least 1/2 hour and then pour it into a buttered and floured ring mold, let it rise again and bake in good oven heat.
When the cake is done, turn it out and soak it thoroughly with a warm mixture of liqueur, sugar and water and let it cool.

Glaze the cake, place it on cake paper on a dish and fill the inside high with glace, preferably some red such as strawberry or raspberry glace. It can also be served with apple or pear compote and can in that case be soaked with the fruit juice instead of the liqueur mixture.

title: Fin fiskfärs (Fine Fish Forcemeat)
description: Prepared with pike, cream, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 1.4 kg pike (= 600 g scraped fish meat)

steps: Take the pike (do not scale), rinse and dry well, fillet it and scrape the fish meat from skin and bones

Force the scraped fish together with the butter three times through a meat grinder and then pound with the egg yolks in a mortar until the mass becomes fine and cohesive
In a bowl mix the cream, salt, sugar, white pepper and sifted flour
Work the mixture into the forcemeat tablespoon by tablespoon
Work the forcemeat for 1 hour, then pass it through a sieve
Finally fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks
Test the forcemeat and pour into well-buttered and bread-crumbed molds
These should not be filled more than halfway and should preferably have lids
If the molds lack lids, cover with buttered paper
Cook the forcemeat in a water bath for 1 hour

title: Fin smördeg (Fine Butter Dough)
description: Prepared with butter, wheat flour, and brandy.

ingredients.name: 1 kg butter (equal weight to the remaining dough)

steps: Make a smooth dough from the flour, water, brandy, and egg, and roll it out in a square to approximately 15 mm thickness.
Place the well-washed butter in the middle.
Fold all four corners of the dough over the butter, and gently clap it out with a rolling pin to a square of approximately 10-15 mm thickness.
Fold this square so that 1/4 is folded inward from the left and 1/4 is folded inward from the right.
The edges of these two folds meet in the middle of the square.
Fold one half of the dough over the other lengthwise.
The dough now has four layers on top of each other.
Fold the long, narrow dough into three parts on top of each other (so you get nine layers).
Work the dough until all the butter is well incorporated, then place it on ice to rest for 20 minutes.
Roll out the dough again to a square of approximately 5-7 mm thickness, fold it together in the same way as before and let it rest on ice for 20 minutes.
Roll it out again and fold it as before.
Then place the dough with the triple-folded side toward you and roll it out in one direction from bottom to top, but fold it together only in three parts.
Do this twice more with 20 minutes rest between each time.
The butter dough is now ready, but should preferably rest a while longer before it is baked out.

title: Fint vingelé (Fine Wine Jelly)
description: Prepared with wine, gelatin, and egg whites.
steps: Rinse the gelatin well in cold water and dissolve it in the hot water, add the lemon zest (from which all the white has been removed), lemon juice and sugar, and bring the mixture to a boil and let it stand 10 minutes beside the stove.

Whip the egg whites in a well-scoured saucepan together with the French wine, and add the gelatin mixture under vigorous whipping. Move the saucepan over the heat and whip the jelly vigorously until it comes to a boil, then cover and let the saucepan stand on the stovetop for 10 minutes without boiling.

Pour the jelly into a stretched cheesecloth, previously wrung out in hot water, and let it drip through. As long as the jelly runs turbid through, pour it back into the cheesecloth. When the jelly is clear, add the Rhine wine or sherry.

Treat the jelly as described above. Serve with almond shavings or almond sprits. If desired, 200 gr. fresh grapes can be placed in the mold. Pour a little jelly on the bottom and let it set, then place some grapes, then jelly again to set, and grapes over, until the mold is full. While the mold is being filled, the remaining jelly must be kept warm.

title: Fiskbuljong (Fish Broth)
description: A soup made with sole or cod or whiting or bones, onion, and juice.

ingredients.name: 8 hectograms sole, cod, or whiting, or raw remnants and bones thereof
1 hectogram fresh or preserved caviar (for clarifying)

steps: For fish broth, use only saltwater fish; sole, cod, and whiting are best, but if necessary, half the weight may be replaced with flounder.
Clean, wash, and dry the fish, then cut it into pieces. If using remnants and bones, wash them well and let them drain.
Peel the onion, blanch it (place in boiling salted water and cook 5 minutes without a lid), and cut into slices.
Clean and wash the parsley and wrap it in cloth.
Butter a heavy-bottomed pot; place the onion, parsley, and fish in it.
Add the lemon juice, cover the pot, place it over low heat, and let it stand for about 15 minutes, shaking it often.
Add the wine and let the liquid reduce by half without a lid, then pour in the cold water.
Skim the broth well, add the spices, and let it simmer gently with a tight lid for about 20 minutes.
Strain through a sieve and let cool, then clarify.
Pound the caviar finely in a mortar with a wooden pestle and mix with the cold broth; pour the mixture into a pot and place over fresh heat.
Stir the broth until it reaches boiling point, then move it to the side of the stove and let it simmer gently with a lid for 20 minutes, then strain carefully.

title: Fiskfärs Timbal (Fish Forcemeat Timbal)
description: Prepared with fish, pike, and cream.

ingredients.name: 3 hectograms shrimp or 1 can lobster (1/2 litre)

steps: Clean and rinse the fish well, cut into fillets and remove the skin.
Pound the fillets with a damp meat mallet until even, rub with salt and vinegar and let rest 1 hour.
Take the pike for the forcemeat, rinse well and dry with a fish towel.
Fillet the fish, scrape the meat finely ensuring no scales or bones are included.
Mix the fish meat with butter and pass through a meat grinder 3 times.
Pound the mixture in a stone mortar with a wooden pestle until fine and cohesive.
Mix flour, cream, eggs and seasonings in a bowl.
Work this mixture into the forcemeat by the tablespoon, stirring for about 1/2 hour.
Butter a smooth timbal mold holding about 1 1/2 litres well.
Wrap the fish fillets in a fish towel and line the mold internally with them, laying them side by side with their tails around the bottom and opposite ends protruding above the rim.
Press well so they take the mold's shape.
Cover the fillets with a 2 cm thick layer of fish forcemeat.
Place the mold in regular oven heat and let stand 10-15 minutes until the forcemeat sets to the fillets.
Cut off the protruding fillet pieces and fill the timbal with the stew to about 3 cm from the top edge.
Lay the cut fish pieces on top of the stew and cover the timbal with a layer of fish forcemeat.
Bake about 45 minutes in a water bath in regular oven heat.

After removing the timbal from the oven, let it rest 10 minutes, then turn out onto a round platter, remove the mold and garnish the top with shrimp tails and truffle slices and around it with parsley or salad.
Serve with crayfish sauce as a course.
For the stew: Clean the shrimp; if using lobster, cut into pieces.
Cut mushrooms and truffles into slices and sauté in butter.
Sauté the crayfish butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream and let the sauce simmer 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp, oysters and mushrooms and bring to a boil, add the beaten egg yolks and season the stew with seasonings.

ingredients.name: 1 kg pike or coalfish (= 400 g scraped fish meat)

Fillet it and scrape the fish meat from skin and bones; no scale or bone should be included

Soften the wheat bread in part of the milk and pass through a sieve

title: Formlimpbröd (Molded Rye Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with rye flour, wheat flour, and syrup.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little cold milk.
Sift the rye flour and wheat flour and mix together with the spices in a large bowl.
Stir the cold milk into the flour, and work the dough until it is supple and shiny.

Sprinkle a little flour over the dough, cover it with a cloth and let it stand in ordinary room temperature to rise for about 24 hours.
Work the well-risen dough and place it in buttered and floured bread molds.
Fill the molds to just under half and place in a warm room to rise.
When the dough has risen to the edge of the mold, place the molds in a good oven heat, and let the breads bake for 2 1/2–3 hours.
After the bread has been in the oven for 1 hour, maintain the fire with only one piece of wood at a time.

steps: Sift the flour into a bowl and set aside a little of it for finishing.

title: Frysning av Glace (Freezing of Glace/Ice Cream)
description: Prepared with ice, saltpeter, and salt.

ingredients.name: saltpeter (12 kg. ice, 1 1/2 kg. coarse salt, 250 gr. saltpeter)

steps: The ice is chopped into pieces, placed in a sack and crushed with a wooden club.
The container is placed in the middle of the tub, ensuring that the turning pin in the middle of the container fits into the corresponding sleeve at the bottom of the wooden tub.

The stirrer is inserted, the lid is placed, the cross beam with the handle is screwed fast, and the ice mixture is then packed around the container with a wooden stick or wooden shovel, but no more than to two-thirds of the container's height, otherwise the salted ice can easily enter the container while the glace freezes.
The container should be frozen down if possible at latest 10 minutes before the glace cream is poured in.
The cold glace mixture is poured in, but must not fill the container to more than two-thirds.
The lid is placed, the handle is screwed fast, and the glace is then turned continuously for 15-30 minutes, depending on whether it is cream glace or fruit glace that is to be frozen.

After the glace is frozen in the aforementioned manner, it can be directly served with a spoon in glasses or in a pyramid on a dish with napkin or cake paper, but it gains in goodness if it is allowed to stand 1-2 hours to "ripen".
The glace mixture can also be filled in the mold and frozen directly in it, such as parfait, frozen pudding, bombe and others.

When the glace is to be served, the mold is taken out of the ice, rinsed thoroughly to remove all salt, dipped for a moment in lukewarm water so that the glace loosens easily from the mold, the mold is dried, and the glace is turned out onto a dish or platter with napkin or cake paper.
